method: Rebuild from primary text, from an independent reading of Health & Safety Code chapter 6.6 rather than by propagation from msa_ca_prop65. The previous record for this clause said in terms: 'Implicated by the confirmed defect in msa_ca_prop65 and checked against the evidence already recorded there; no new search.' A propagated verdict is not a verification. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Health & Safety Code ch. 6.6 full text (leginfo)
Lee v. Amazon.com Proposition 65 constructive knowledge

assertions.text: a business employing fewer than ten people is outside 'person in the course of doing business' and owes no warning
assertions.note: §25249.11(b). Now the first sentence of the clause, because it decides whether the rest of it applies at all.

assertions.text: the list of chemicals is updated through the year
assertions.note: §25249.8 requires the list to be published and revised at least once per year. The annual review cadence the clause prescribes is this corpus's operational choice, not a statutory one — see gaps.

assertions.text: constructive knowledge suffices, so having failed to look is not a defence
assertions.note: Lee v. Amazon.com. This is the reason a periodic review is worth doing at all, and it was absent from the previous body.

assertions.text: a non-conforming warning loses the safe harbour rather than being void
assertions.note: See the msa_ca_prop65 finding. The statutory standard is 'clear and reasonable'; the safe harbour is regulatory and could not be read.

assertions.text: private enforcement requires 60 days' notice with a certificate of merit and no diligently prosecuting public prosecutor
exposure is up to $2,500 per day per violation, assessed against seven factors including good faith measures and when they were taken
assertions.note: §25249.7(b)(1)-(2). This is the provision that gives a documented review programme its value, and it is why the clause now names it.

priorDefects: overstated: 'A warning that is present but non-conforming is treated as no warning.' Propagated from msa_ca_prop65.
omitted: the fewer-than-ten-employees exclusion. Propagated from msa_ca_prop65.
omitted: the knowledge element and its constructive-knowledge construction.
omitted: the certificate of merit and the diligent-prosecution bar, which are what a 60-day notice has to satisfy.
omitted: the penalty figure and the seven factors — including the good-faith-measures factor that is the whole payoff of a review clause.
unsupported: 'private plaintiffs who recover attorney's fees'. No fee provision was found in chapter 6.6.
method: the previous record was not an independent check and said so.
gaps: The annual cadence is a housekeeping choice, not a statutory requirement, and no source read here says annually is enough. The clause presents it alongside statutory rules and a reader will not tell them apart.

The Article 6 safe-harbour regulations were never opened — govt.westlaw.com returns HTTP 403 and the agency hosts oehha.ca.gov and p65warnings.ca.gov return a firewall challenge — so what a 'correctly worded' warning is cannot be stated, which is most of what this review is supposed to check.
The internet-purchase placement rule is in Article 6 and was not read.
Whether a private plaintiff recovers fees, and under what provision, was not verified.

judicialQuotations.case: Lee v. Amazon.com, Inc. (Cal. Ct. App. 2022)
judicialQuotations.quote: Interpreting section 25249.6 to require warnings only when a person in the course of doing business has actual knowledge that he or she will expose any individual to a listed chemical would significantly limit the reach of the statute and create incentives to avoid information that might reveal potential sources of exposure.
